claim: KPC-1 is a C. elegans Furin homolog that regulates the level of the branching receptor DMA-1 on dendrites by targeting it to late endosomes.
source: Here, we show that KPC-1, a C. elegans Furin homolog, regulates the level of the branching receptor DMA-1 on dendrites by targeting it to late endosomes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: In kpc-1 mutants, the level of DMA-1 is abnormally high on dendrites.
source: In kpc-1 mutants, the level of DMA-1 is abnormally high on dendrites, resulting in trapping of dendrites at locations where a high level of the cognate ligand, the adhesion molecule SAX-7/L1, is present.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Abnormally high DMA-1 levels in kpc-1 mutants result in trapping of dendrites at locations where a high level of SAX-7/L1 is present.
source: In kpc-1 mutants, the level of DMA-1 is abnormally high on dendrites, resulting in trapping of dendrites at locations where a high level of the cognate ligand, the adhesion molecule SAX-7/L1, is present.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through genetic and imaging experiments in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The misregulation of DMA-1 causes dendritic self-avoidance defects.
source: The misregulation of DMA-1 also causes dendritic self-avoidance defects.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3 and Figure 5.

claim: Precise regulation of guidance receptors creates flexibility of responses to guidance signals and is critical for neuronal morphogenesis.
source: Thus, precise regulation of guidance receptors creates flexibility of responses to guidance signals and is critical for neuronal morphogenesis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, drawing from the experimental findings.

claim: SAX-7 is the ortholog of the vertebrate neuronal adhesion molecule L1CAM.
source: SAX-7 is the ortholog of the vertebrate neuronal adhesion molecule L1CAM (Zallen et al., 1999; Chen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from previous literature.

claim: PVD neurons first grow two longitudinally extending 1° dendrites, from which numerous 2° dendrites emerge roughly perpendicular to the 1° dendrites.
source: PVD neurons first grow two longitudinally extending 1° dendrites, from which numerous 2° dendrites emerge roughly perpendicular to the 1° dendrites (Smith et al., 2010; Albeg et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the morphology of PVD neurons with citation support.

claim: Upon reaching two sublateral lines where SAX-7 is highly enriched, PVD dendrites form stereotyped 'T'-shaped 3° branches.
source: Upon reaching two sublateral lines where the guidance molecule SAX-7 is highly enriched (arrows in Figure 1A), the PVD dendrites form stereotyped 'T'-shaped 3° branches.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SAX-7 and MNR-1 are both necessary and sufficient to instruct dendrite morphogenesis through direct interactions with the PVD receptor DMA-1.
source: SAX-7 and MNR-1 are both necessary and sufficient to instruct dendrite morphogenesis through direct interactions with the PVD receptor DMA-1 (Liu and Shen, 2012; Dong et al., 2013; Salzberg et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from previous studies.

claim: SAX-7, MNR-1 and DMA-1 form a tripartite ligand-receptor signaling complex that enables stereotyped dendritic branch formation and stabilization.
source: SAX-7, MNR-1 and DMA-1 form a tripartite ligand-receptor signaling complex that enables stereotyped dendritic branch formation and stabilization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on previous work.

claim: In addition to the sublateral stripes where 3° branches form, SAX-7 was also enriched in a zone that roughly lined up with the 1° branches.
source: A close examination of SAX-7 localization revealed that, in addition to the sublateral stripes where 3° branches form, SAX-7 was also enriched in a zone that roughly lined up with the 1° branches (Figure 1A, arrowhead) (Dong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SAX-7 is expressed and localized well before PVD dendrite morphogenesis begins.
source: Since SAX-7 is expressed and localized well before PVD dendrite morphogenesis begins (Dong et al., 2013), the 2° dendrites encounter the SAX-7 domain as they emerge from the 1° dendrite.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: In wild-type animals, the vast majority of 2° dendrites grow out of the SAX-7 domain to reach the sublateral line and form 3° branches there.
source: In wild-type animals, the vast majority of 2° dendrites grow out of the SAX-7 domain to reach the sublateral line and form 3° branches there.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In kpc-1 mutants, almost all 2° branches failed to grow out of the trap zone between the dotted lines indicated by enriched SAX-7.
source: In kpc-1(gk8) mutants, almost all branches failed to grow out of the trap zone between the dotted lines indicated by enriched SAX-7.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 1B and shown in the image.

claim: Expressing KPC-1 during L2 failed to rescue the kpc-1(gk8) mutant phenotype.
source: Expressing KPC-1 during L2 failed to rescue the kpc-1(gk8) mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 caption and shown in the data.

claim: Expressing KPC-1 during early L3 completely rescued the kpc-1(gk8) mutant phenotype.
source: Expressing KPC-1 during early L3 completely rescued the mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 caption and shown in the data.

claim: Expressing KPC-1 during L4 or later stages could partially rescue some menorahs, but still many branches were trapped in the trap zone.
source: Expressing KPC-1 during L4 or later stages could partially rescue some menorahs, but still many branches were trapped in the trap zone.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 caption and shown in the data.

claim: KPC-1 was required during a stringent time window when the 2° branches synchronously bypassed the high level SAX-7 region to allow proper outgrowth.
source: These results agreed with a previous report using temporal RNAi (Salzberg et al., 2014) and demonstrated that KPC-1 was required during a stringent time window when the 2° branches synchronously bypassed the high level SAX-7 region to allow proper outgrowth.
evidence: This is stated based on the temporal expression experiments and cited previous work.

claim: Mutations in the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 complex were epistatic to kpc-1 mutations.
source: Genetic analyses showed that mutations in the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 complex were epistatic to kpc-1 mutations (Schroeder et al., 2013; Salzberg et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from previous studies.

claim: The kpc-1; sax-7, kpc-1; mnr-1 and kpc-1; dma-1 double mutants showed PVD morphologies indistinguishable from those of the sax-7, mnr-1 or dma-1 single mutants.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Schroeder et al., 2013; Salzberg et al., 2014), we observed that the kpc-1; sax-7, kpc-1; mnr-1 and kpc-1; dma-1 double mutants showed PVD morphologies indistinguishable from those of the sax-7, mnr-1 or dma-1 single mutants (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation support and shown in Figure 2 and supplementary figures.

claim: The percentages of trapped dendrites in the double mutants were comparable to those of single mutants of the tripartite complex but were significantly lower than that in the kpc-1 single mutants.
source: Nevertheless, the percentages of trapped dendrites in the double mutants were comparable to those of single mutants of the tripartite complex but were significantly lower than that in the kpc-1 single mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Defects in the kpc-1 mutants arose as a result of ectopic activation of ligand-receptor signaling near the seam cells.
source: This result suggested that defects in the kpc-1 mutants arose as a result of ectopic activation of ligand-receptor signaling near the seam cells.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the genetic epistasis results.

claim: Expressing SAX-7 in the seam cells restored the trapping phenotype in kpc-1; sax-7 double mutants.
source: In striking contrast to the double mutants themselves (Figure 2B), the PVD dendrites in the kpc-1; sax-7 double mutants expressing SAX-7 in seam cells were trapped in the seam cell area, with very few 2° branches reaching far from the 1° dendrite (Figure 2C,G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C and 2G.

claim: The dendritic trapping phenotype in the kpc-1 mutants was due to the excessive activity of the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 complex near the seam cells.
source: These results further supported the notion that the dendritic trapping phenotype in the kpc-1 mutants was due to the excessive activity of the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 complex near the seam cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ectopic expression experiments.

claim: Ectopic expression of SAX-7 and MNR-1 in the ALM and PLM neurons in the sax-7; kpc-1 double mutants caused the entire PVD dendritic arbor to follow the PLM and ALM neurites.
source: We also ectopically expressed SAX-7 and MNR-1 in the ALM and PLM neurons in the sax-7; kpc-1 double mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 3). ALM and PLM neurons have long neurites that extend in the dorsal and ventral sublateral nerve cords and overlap with the locations where PVD 3° branches form and grow. This ectopic expression converted the sax-7 mutant-like dendritic pattern (Figure 2B) to a striking new pattern: the entire PVD dendritic arbor followed the PLM and ALM neurites (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Providing DMA-1 during early L3 in dma-1; kpc-1 mutants led to robust restoration of the trapping phenotype.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, providing DMA-1 during early L3 when the 2° branches grew within the trap zone led to robust restoration of the trapping phenotype (Figure 2E,H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E and 2H.

claim: Expressing DMA-1 at later time points in dma-1; kpc-1 mutants, when most of the branches had already extended beyond the trapping zone, led to a striking rescue of 3° and 4° branches.
source: On the contrary, expressing DMA-1 at later time points, when most of the branches in dma-1 mutants had already extended beyond the trapping zone, led to a striking rescue of 3° and 4° branches (Figure 2F,H), again demonstrating strongly that dendrites in the kpc-1 mutants did not lack outgrowth capability and maintained intact SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F and 2H.

claim: Dendrites in the kpc-1 mutants did not lack outgrowth capability and maintained intact SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 signaling.
source: On the contrary, expressing DMA-1 at later time points, when most of the branches in dma-1 mutants had already extended beyond the trapping zone, led to a striking rescue of 3° and 4° branches (Figure 2F,H), again demonstrating strongly that dendrites in the kpc-1 mutants did not lack outgrowth capability and maintained intact SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 signaling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the temporal rescue experiments.

claim: The kpc-1 mutant PVD dendrites responded excessively to the guidance cues SAX-7 and MNR-1 near the seam cells, which limited their growth to the 'trap zone'.
source: Instead, the kpc-1 mutant PVD dendrites responded excessively to the guidance cues SAX-7 and MNR-1 near the seam cells, which limited their growth to the 'trap zone'.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the genetic and temporal experiments.

claim: The kpc-1(xr58) allele resulted in an amino acid substitution P440S.
source: In an independent genetic screen for mutants with PVD dendrite self-avoidance defects, we isolated another allele of kpc-1, xr58, which resulted in an amino acid substitution P440S (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The PVD neurons of the kpc-1(xr58) mutants showed a fully penetrant, complex phenotype.
source: Unlike a previously reported mutation of the same amino acid (kpc-1(my24), P440L) which gave rise to a null phenotype, the PVD neurons of the kpc-1(xr58) mutants showed a fully penetrant, complex phenotype (Figure 3B) (Schroeder et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Some 2° dendrites in kpc-1(xr58) mutants were trapped near the 1° dendrites.
source: Similar to the complete loss-of-function kpc-1(gk8) mutants (Figure 1B, 3D), some 2° dendrites in kpc-1(xr58) mutants were trapped near the 1° dendrites (Figure 3B, asterisks, Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 2° dendrite trapping phenotype in kpc-1(xr58) was much weaker than that in the gk8 allele yet significantly different from that in the wild-type animals.
source: The 2° dendrite trapping phenotype was much weaker than that in the gk8 allele yet significantly different from that in the wild-type animals (Figure 1C, 3A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C and Figure 3.

claim: Many 2° dendrites in the kpc-1(xr58) mutants, especially those in the proximal region near the cell body, could successfully extend away from the 1° dendrite and formed full menorahs with T-shaped 3° branches and many 4° branches on them.
source: Unlike the PVD dendrites of the kpc-1 null mutants, which failed to make any intact menorahs, many 2° dendrites in the kpc-1(xr58) mutants, especially those in the proximal region near the cell body, could successfully extend away from the 1° dendrite and formed full menorahs with T-shaped 3° branches and many 4° branches on them.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the phenotype.

claim: The 3° branches in kpc-1(xr58) mutants had a striking self-avoidance defect.
source: However, the 3° branches in this mutant had a striking self-avoidance defect (Figure 3B, arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In wild-type animals, 3° branches showed stringent self-avoidance, with neighboring 3° dendrites almost never overlapping with each other and instead showing gaps in between.
source: In wild-type animals, 3° branches showed stringent self-avoidance. Neighboring 3° dendrites almost never overlapped with each other and instead showed gaps in between (Figure 3A, arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Around 70% of 3° branches had self-avoidance defects in the kpc-1(xr58) mutants, compared to only 2% in wild-type worms.
source: We quantified the percentage of 'T'-shaped 3° dendrites that made contact with their neighbors and found that around 70% of 3° branches had self-avoidance defects in the kpc-1(xr58) mutants, compared to only 2% in wild-type worms (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: kpc-1(xr58) had a reduced number of 4° branches, with 4° dendrites largely absent from the menorahs except in the most proximal menorah.
source: In addition to the self-avoidance defects of the 3° branches, kpc-1(xr58) also had a reduced number of 4° branches. Except in the most proximal menorah (closest to the cell body), the 4° dendrites were largely absent from the menorahs (Figure 3B, stars, Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B and Figure 5D.

claim: SAX-7 was highly enriched in the sublateral lines where 3° branches formed and grew and was also localized to vertical stripes followed by the 4° branches but at much lower concentration.
source: SAX-7 was highly enriched in the sublateral lines where 3° branches formed and grew and was also localized to vertical stripes followed by the 4° branches but at much lower concentration.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 3E-F and shown in the images.

claim: kpc-1(xr58) was a partial loss-of-function allele of kpc-1.
source: Several lines of evidence suggested that kpc-1(xr58) was a partial loss-of-function allele of kpc-1.
evidence: This is stated based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the text.

claim: kpc-1(xr58) had a missense point mutation in the catalytic domain of KPC-1, which likely affected its protease function.
source: First, KPC-1 encodes a conserved proprotein convertase and is a homolog of mammalian Furin (Schroeder et al., 2013; Hung et al., 2014). kpc-1(xr58) had a missense point mutation in the catalytic domain of KPC-1, which likely affected its protease function.
evidence: This is stated with citation support and inference about the mutation's effect.

claim: Injecting a mutated version of kpc-1 cDNA containing the P440S mutation into the null kpc-1(gk8) deletion mutants produced a dendritic phenotype that was milder than gk8 but indistinguishable from that of kpc-1(xr58).
source: Injecting a mutated version of kpc-1 cDNA containing the P440S mutation into the null kpc-1(gk8) deletion mutants produced a dendritic phenotype that was milder than gk8 but indistinguishable from that of kpc-1(xr58), suggesting that the xr58 allele was a hypomorphic allele (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text as experimental evidence.

claim: Expressing the wild-type kpc-1 cDNA at a very low concentration in the kpc-1(gk8) null allele resulted in a PVD morphology that was similar to that of the xr58 mutants.
source: Second, expressing the wild-type kpc-1 cDNA at a very low concentration in the kpc-1(gk8) null allele resulted in a PVD morphology that was similar to that of the xr58 mutants (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C and supplementary figures.

claim: RNAi against kpc-1 gave rise to a similar PVD dendritic phenotype to that of xr58.
source: Third, RNAi against kpc-1 also gave rise to a similar PVD dendritic phenotype to that of xr58 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text as experimental evidence.

claim: The full activation of mammalian Furin requires proteolytic cleavage of its N-terminal Pro domain by its own catalytic domain.
source: The full activation of mammalian Furin requires proteolytic cleavage of its N-terminal Pro domain by its own catalytic domain (Thomas, 2002).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: When the worm KPC-1 was expressed in cultured Drosophila S2 cells, two protein products were found that corresponded to full-length and Pro domain-cleaved KPC-1 based on size.
source: Indeed, when the worm KPC-1 was expressed in cultured Drosophila S2 cells, we found two protein products that corresponded to full-length and Pro domain-cleaved KPC-1 based on size (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Mutating both putative cleavage sites in KPC-1 with R to A mutations completely lacked the self-cleavage product when expressed in S2 cells.
source: We mutated both sites with R to A mutations and found that the resulting mutant protein completely lacked the self-cleavage product when expressed in S2 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), suggesting that these two sites were indeed responsible for the self-cleavage of KPC-1.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Introducing R136A and R143A mutations into the endogenous kpc-1 locus using CRISPR/Cas9 resulted in mutants that exhibited a PVD dendritic phenotype indistinguishable from that of the gk8 null mutants.
source: To assess the physiological function of these cleavage sites, we introduced these two mutations into the endogenous kpc-1 locus using the CRISPR/Cas9 system (Paix et al., 2014). The mutants exhibited a PVD dendritic phenotype indistinguishable from that of the gk8 null mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating the necessity of Pro domain cleavage for the activation of KPC-1.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: KPC-1 lacking the Pro domain could fully rescue the gk8 mutants.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, KPC-1 lacking the Pro domain could fully rescue the gk8 mutants. Both secondary trapping and menorah outgrowth phenotypes were restored to wild-type level (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, D, and E.

claim: KPC-1ΔProP440S fully rescued the 2° branch trapping phenotype in kpc-1(xr58) mutants.
source: KPC-1ΔProP440S fully rescued the 2° branch trapping phenotype (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D) and partially restored the number of 4° branches (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D, and E.

claim: Similar to mammalian Furin, KPC-1 also needed to cleave its own Pro domain to be fully activated.
source: This was consistent with our model that, similar to mammalian Furin, KPC-1 also needed to cleave its own Pro domain to be fully activated.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the Pro domain deletion experiments.

claim: The dendritic morphology of the kpc-1(xr58) mutant was reminiscent of the phenotype caused by overexpression of DMA-1 in PVD.
source: The dendritic morphology of the kpc-1(xr58) mutant was reminiscent of the phenotype caused by overexpression of DMA-1 in PVD (Figure 5A) (Liu and Shen, 2012):
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Neurons overexpressing DMA-1 had severe self-avoidance defects, with 3° dendrites often failing to avoid each other and forming a continuous fascicle that covered the entire sublateral line.
source: First, neurons overexpressing DMA-1 had severe self-avoidance defects. Their 3° dendrites often failed to avoid each other and formed a continuous fascicle that covered the entire sublateral line (Figure 5A, arrowheads, Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and 5C.

claim: In neurons overexpressing DMA-1, many 2° dendrites were trapped around the 1° dendrite.
source: In addition, many 2° dendrites were trapped around the 1° dendrite (Figure 5A, asterisks, Figure 1C), and the total number of 4° branches was decreased (Figure 5A, star, Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and Figure 1C.

claim: In neurons overexpressing DMA-1, the total number of 4° branches was decreased.
source: In addition, many 2° dendrites were trapped around the 1° dendrite (Figure 5A, asterisks, Figure 1C), and the total number of 4° branches was decreased (Figure 5A, star, Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5D.

claim: Both KPC-1 and DMA-1 functioned autonomously in the PVD neuron.
source: Since both KPC-1 and DMA-1 functioned autonomously in the PVD neuron, we hypothesized that KPC-1 might affect the PVD dendrites through regulating DMA-1.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on previous findings.

claim: In wild-type animals, diffuse DMA-1-GFP fluorescence was localized to all dendritic compartments including the higher order branches.
source: In wild-type animals, diffuse DMA-1-GFP fluorescence was localized to all dendritic compartments including the higher order branches (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Discrete GFP puncta could be found in the cell body and 1° dendrites of wild-type PVD, which were likely secretory or endocytic vesicles that carry DMA-1.
source: Discrete GFP puncta could also be found in the cell body and 1° dendrites, which were likely secretory or endocytic vesicles that carry DMA-1 (Figure 4A, right panel).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In wild-type neurons, DMA-1-GFP intensity in the discrete puncta was significantly higher than the diffuse staining in the dendrites.
source: In wild-type neurons, DMA-1-GFP intensity in the discrete puncta was significantly higher than the diffuse staining in the dendrites (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In the kpc-1(gk8) mutants, a striking increase in the diffuse DMA-1-GFP intensity in the entire dendritic arbor was observed.
source: In the kpc-1(gk8) mutants, we observed a striking increase in the diffuse DMA-1-GFP intensity in the entire dendritic arbor (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Quantification of the brightness of diffuse DMA-1-GFP on the dendrite showed a dramatic increase in the kpc-1(gk8) allele compared with wild-type.
source: Quantification of the brightness of diffuse DMA-1-GFP on the dendrite, which was likely membrane-localized DMA-1-GFP, showed a dramatic increase in the kpc-1(gk8) allele compared with wild-type (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A similar but less dramatic increase in DMA-1-GFP intensity was observed for the weak allele kpc-1(xr58).
source: A similar but less dramatic increase in DMA-1-GFP intensity was observed for the weak allele kpc-1(xr58) as well (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The up-regulation of DMA-1-GFP in kpc-1 mutants could be completely rescued by PVD autonomous expression of KPC-1.
source: Such up-regulation could be completely rescued by PVD autonomous expression of KPC-1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Western blot analysis confirmed that there was indeed an overall increase in DMA-1 protein level in the kpc-1 mutants.
source: To quantify the total DMA-1-GFP protein level, we performed Western blot analysis using an antibody against GFP and confirmed that there was indeed an overall increase in DMA-1 protein level in the kpc-1 mutants (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Endogenous DMA-1 tagged with YFP using CRISPR showed dramatic increase in DMA-1-YFP intensity in kpc-1(gk8) double mutants.
source: Furthermore, we monitored endogenous DMA-1 by engineering a YFP into the dma-1 genomic locus using CRISPR (Paix et al., 2014). Despite dim fluorescence intensity, we were able to visualize the endogenous expression and observed a DMA-1 localization pattern similar to what we saw using high copy transgenes, with both membrane and vesicular distribution of the protein (data not shown). When we crossed the dma-1::yfp knockin strain into kpc-1(gk8), we again observed dramatic increase in DMA-1-YFP intensity in the double mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A 2xFLAG tag inserted into the endogenous locus of dma-1 using CRISPR showed significant up-regulation of DMA-1 protein level in kpc-1 mutants.
source: Similarly, a 2xFLAG tag was inserted in frame into the endogenous locus of dma-1 using CRISPR (Paix et al., 2014), and we again measured significant up-regulation of DMA-1 protein level in kpc-1 mutants (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: The level of HPO-30 on the membrane was not changed in kpc-1 mutants.
source: As a control, we examined the fluorescent intensity and localization of HPO-30, another transmembrane protein important for PVD development (Smith et al., 2013), and observed no significant change in its dendritic levels in the kpc-1(gk8) mutants despite severe morphology defects (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: There was no difference in dma-1 transcript level between wild-type and kpc-1(gk8) mutants.
source: We also performed qPCR and found that there was no difference in dma-1 transcript level between wild-type and kpc-1(gk8) mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: KPC-1 specifically down-regulated the DMA-1 protein level without affecting transcription.
source: These results further supported the notion that KPC-1 specifically down-regulated the DMA-1 protein level without affecting transcription.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the qPCR and protein level measurements.

claim: Overexpressing DMA-1 in the kpc-1(xr58) allele further enhanced the dendritic phenotypes.
source: First, overexpressing DMA-1 in the kpc-1(xr58) allele further enhanced the dendritic phenotypes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Overexpression of a truncated version of DMA-1 lacking its entire cytosolic domain generated a dramatic trapping phenotype that mimicked that of the kpc-1(gk8) null mutant.
source: Second, we found that overexpression of a truncated version of DMA-1 lacking its entire cytosolic domain generated a dramatic trapping phenotype that mimicked that of the kpc-1(gk8) null mutant (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The cytosolic domain of DMA-1 may contain signaling motifs that were important for its endocytosis.
source: We suspected that the cytosolic domain of DMA-1 may contain signaling motifs that were important for its endocytosis, so overexpressing a DMA-1 construct which lacked these motifs led to higher level of DMA-1 on the dendritic membrane than overexpression of the full length DMA-1 did, thereby produced a more severe trapping phenotype.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis to explain the observed phenotype.

claim: A dma-1 mutant allele lacking its cytosolic domain generated using CRISPR/Cas9 showed that 2° and 3° branches developed normally, suggesting that this truncated protein was partially functional.
source: We also generated a similar mutant allele of dma-1 lacking its cytosolic domain using the CRISPR/Cas9 system (Friedland et al., 2013) and observed a similar phenotype. 2° and 3° branches of these mutants developed normally, suggesting that this truncated protein was partially functional (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: Removing KPC-1 in the dma-1 cytosolic deletion background resulted in a severe trapping phenotype.
source: Interestingly, removing KPC-1 in this genetic background resulted in a severe trapping phenotype, indicating that KPC-1 did not regulate DMA-1 through its cytosolic domain and that the extracellular domain of DMA-1 was sufficient to respond to SAX-7/MNR-1 and to generate trapping (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: KPC-1 did not regulate DMA-1 through its cytosolic domain and the extracellular domain of DMA-1 was sufficient to respond to SAX-7/MNR-1 and to generate trapping.
source: Interestingly, removing KPC-1 in this genetic background resulted in a severe trapping phenotype, indicating that KPC-1 did not regulate DMA-1 through its cytosolic domain and that the extracellular domain of DMA-1 was sufficient to respond to SAX-7/MNR-1 and to generate trapping (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiment.

claim: The overabundance of the DMA-1 receptor was responsible for the phenotypes in the loss-of-function alleles of kpc-1.
source: The striking similarity between the kpc-1 null and the strain overexpressing the truncated DMA-1 shown in Figure 5E, together with the observation that the loss of DMA-1 suppressed the trapping phenotype of the kpc-1(gk8) mutant allele, argued strongly that the overabundance of the DMA-1 receptor was responsible for the phenotypes in the loss-of-function alleles of kpc-1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from multiple genetic experiments.

claim: When DMA-1-RFP expressing cells were mixed with cells co-expressing SAX-7-GFP and MNR-1-GFP, the red and green cells formed clusters that indicated direct interaction between the DMA-1 receptor and the SAX-7/MNR-1 complex in trans.
source: As we have reported previously, when DMA-1-RFP expressing cells were mixed with cells co-expressing SAX-7-GFP and MNR-1-GFP, the red and green cells formed clusters that indicated direct interaction between the DMA-1 receptor and the SAX-7/MNR-1 complex in trans (Figure 6A, arrows, Figure 6C) (Dong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and shown in Figure 6A and 6C.

claim: Co-transfection of KPC-1 with DMA-1 in the same cells completely blocked cell aggregation.
source: Co-transfection of KPC-1 with DMA-1 in the same cells completely blocked cell aggregation (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: The DMA-1 level was diminished in cells co-expressing KPC-1.
source: We then directly examined the amount of DMA-1 in the cells by probing for Myc-tagged DMA-1 with an anti-Myc antibody on Western blots, and found that, consistent with what we have observed in worms, the DMA-1 level was diminished in the cells co-expressing KPC-1 (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D and 6E.

claim: Another type I transmembrane protein mCD8 was co-transfected in the same cell cultures and was not affected, showing that the effect of KPC-1 on DMA-1 was specific.
source: Another type I transmembrane protein mCD8 was co-transfected in the same cell cultures and was not affected, showing that the effect of KPC-1 on DMA-1 was specific.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a control experiment.

claim: KPC-1 down-regulated DMA-1 not only in worm neurons but also in Drosophila S2 cells.
source: This result showed that KPC-1 down-regulated DMA-1 not only in worm neurons but also in Drosophila S2 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the S2 cell experiments.

claim: DMA-1-RFP alone localized to the plasma membrane in S2R+ cells, which could be seen particularly clearly on the filopodial and lamellipodial structures.
source: DMA-1-RFP alone localized to the plasma membrane, which could be seen particularly clearly on the filopodial and lamellipodial structures (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When KPC-1-CFP was co-transfected with DMA-1-RFP, membrane-localized DMA-1-RFP was diminished.
source: However, when KPC-1-CFP was co-transfected with DMA-1-RFP, membrane-localized DMA-1-RFP was diminished (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The intracellular DMA-1-GFP puncta showed a high degree of co-localization with mCherry-RAB-7 in wild-type PVD neurons.
source: Indeed, the intracellular DMA-1-GFP puncta showed a high degree of co-localization with mCherry-RAB-7 in wild-type PVD neurons (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Around 80% of RAB-7 vesicles co-localized with DMA-1-GFP in wild-type animals.
source: Around 80% of RAB-7 vesicles co-localized with DMA-1-GFP (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: DMA-1 was targeted to late endosomes in wild-type animals.
source: This result indicated that DMA-1 was indeed targeted to late endosomes in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the co-localization experiment.

claim: In kpc-1(gk8) mutant animals, concomitant with the increased DMA-1-GFP level on the dendritic membrane, there was reduced co-localization between DMA-1-GFP and RAB-7 vesicles.
source: In contrast, in kpc-1(gk8) mutant animals, concomitant with the increased DMA-1-GFP level on the dendritic membrane, there was reduced co-localization between DMA-1-GFP and RAB-7 vesicles (Figure 7B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7B and 7E.

claim: DMA-1Δcyto-GFP exhibited much stronger membrane localization when expressed at comparable levels as the full length protein.
source: Indeed, DMA-1Δcyto-GFP exhibited much stronger membrane localization when expressed at comparable levels as the full length protein (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: There was a reduction in the percentage of RAB-7 vesicles containing GFP when DMA-1Δcyto-GFP was expressed.
source: We then quantified the co-localization between mCherry-RAB-7 and DMA-1Δcyto-GFP and observed a reduction in the percentage of RAB-7 vesicles containing GFP (Figure 7C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7C and 7E.

claim: When the integrated transgene expressing DMA-1Δcyto-GFP was crossed into kpc-1(gk8) mutants, the GFP signal appeared almost exclusively on the plasma membrane.
source: Furthermore, when we crossed the integrated transgene expressing DMA-1Δcyto-GFP into kpc-1(gk8) mutants, the GFP signal appeared almost exclusively on the plasma membrane (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Only 10% of late endosomes labeled by mCherry-RAB-7 contained DMA-1Δcyto-GFP in kpc-1(gk8) mutants.
source: Very few vesicles were seen throughout the dendritic arbor and only 10% of late endosomes labeled by mCherry-RAB-7 contained DMA-1Δcyto-GFP (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7D and 7E.

claim: Direct binding between DMA-1 and KPC-1 ectodomains was detected with an apparent dissociation constant of 33 µM using biolayer interferometry.
source: Direct binding between these proteins was detected with an apparent dissociation constant of 33 µM using biolayer interferometry (Figure 7F, blue circles).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7F.

claim: No binding was detected between DMA-1 and the negative control, the ectodomain of human GPR56.
source: No binding was detected between DMA-1 and the negative control, the ectodomain of human GPR56 (Figure 7F, open rectangles).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7F.

claim: KPC-1-CFP showed strong co-localization with Venus-RAB-7 when co-expressed in S2R+ cells.
source: We co-expressed KPC-1-CFP and Venus-RAB-7 in these cells and observed strong co-localization between KPC-1 and RAB-7 (Figure 7G–I, arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7G-I.

claim: KPC-1 bound directly to the ectodomain of DMA-1 and targeted the receptor to late endosomes and lysosomes for degradation.
source: Together, these data were consistent with a model in which KPC-1 bound directly to the ectodomain of DMA-1 and targeted the receptor to late endosomes and lysosomes for degradation (Figure 7J).
evidence: This is stated as the proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: In kpc-1 mutants, the level of DMA-1 was increased on the dendritic plasma membrane, leading to excessive responsiveness to the guidance signals SAX-7 and MNR-1.
source: In kpc-1 mutants, the level of DMA-1 was increased on the dendritic plasma membrane, leading to excessive responsiveness to the guidance signals SAX-7 and MNR-1.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: PVD dendrites became trapped at intermediate targets with enriched SAX-7 and failed to move away as a consequence of increased DMA-1 levels in kpc-1 mutants.
source: Consequently, PVD dendrites became trapped at intermediate targets with enriched SAX-7 and failed to move away.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: The same ligand can trigger a variety of responses in different neuronal types depending on the membrane receptor contents of their growth cones.
source: It has been shown by the classic studies on axon guidance that the same ligand can trigger a variety of responses in different neuronal types depending on the membrane receptor contents of their growth cones.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Netrin functions as a chemoattractant when binding to the UNC-40/DCC receptor but repels axons containing an UNC-5 and UNC-40/DCC receptor complex.
source: Netrin functions as a chemoattractant when binding to the UNC-40/DCC receptor but repels axons containing an UNC-5 and UNC-40/DCC receptor complex (Hedgecock et al., 1990; Tessier-Lavigne and Goodman, 1996; Hong et al., 1999; Powell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: In regions of the nervous system that are wired in a topographic fashion such as the superior colliculus in the visual system, the relative level of Eph receptors dictates where in the Ephrin gradient an axon stops.
source: In regions of the nervous system that are wired in a topographic fashion such as the superior colliculus in the visual system, the relative level of Eph receptors dictates where in the Ephrin gradient an axon stops (Cheng et al., 1995; Wilkinson, 2001; Mann et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: In Drosophila, Comm functions in pre-crossing commissural axons to keep the Robo receptor level low by sorting the receptors into endosomes.
source: In Drosophila, Comm functions in pre-crossing commissural axons to keep the Robo receptor level low by sorting the receptors into endosomes, whereas Comm is turned off after the axon has crossed the midline and the Robo receptor is restored on the surface of growth cones to gain responsiveness to the midline repellent Slit and prevent axons from recrossing (Keleman et al., 2002; Keleman et al., 2005; Dickson and Gilestro, 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: Commissural axons in the mammalian spinal cord change their responses to Slit by altering their expression of the Robo3 splicing isoforms.
source: Similarly, commissural axons in the mammalian spinal cord change their responses to Slit by altering their expression of the Robo3 splicing isoforms. (Sabatier et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: Dynamic regulation of the guidance receptor is required for proper dendrite development.
source: We present a new case in neurite morphogenesis in which dynamic regulation of the guidance receptor is required for proper development.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.

claim: KPC-1/Furin is responsible for down-regulation of the DMA-1 receptor to allow dendrites to move away from an area with enriched SAX-7/MNR-1 ligands.
source: We show that KPC-1/Furin is responsible for down-regulation of the DMA-1 receptor to allow dendrites to move away from an area with enriched SAX-7/MNR-1 ligands.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.

claim: KPC-1 is a worm proprotein convertase known to process and activate proteins and peptides by proteolytic cleavage at a conserved consensus sequence.
source: KPC-1 is a worm proprotein convertase known to process and activate proteins and peptides by proteolytic cleavage at a conserved consensus sequence (Thomas, 2002).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: KPC-1 was shown to be a major convertase to cleave and activate insulin peptides in neurons for the activation of the dauer formation pathway.
source: For example, KPC-1 was shown to be a major convertase to cleave and activate insulin peptides in neurons for the activation of the dauer formation pathway (Hung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from the literature.

claim: KPC-1 functions in multi-dendritic neurons to assist dendritic morphogenesis and is in the same genetic pathway as the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 signaling complex.
source: Our results, like previous studies, indicate that KPC-1 functions in multi-dendritic neurons to assist dendritic morphogenesis and is in the same genetic pathway as the SAX-7/MNR-1/DMA-1 signaling complex (Schroeder et al., 2013; Salzberg et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from previous studies.

claim: The morphological defects of the PVD dendrites in the kpc-1 mutants are due to enhanced, rather than decreased, response to the SAX-7/MNR-1 ligands.
source: However, our results provide strong genetic and cell biological evidence that the morphological defects of the PVD dendrites in the kpc-1 mutants are due to enhanced, rather than decreased, response to the SAX-7/MNR-1 ligands.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.

claim: KPC-1 functioned similarly to another member of the mammalian convertase family, PCSK9, which down-regulated the LDL receptor through directly binding to its extracellular EGF domain and targeting the receptor to the endocytic pathway for degradation.
source: We therefore hypothesized that KPC-1 functioned similarly to another member of the mammalian convertase family, PCSK9, which down-regulated the LDL receptor through directly binding to its extracellular EGF domain and targeting the receptor to the endocytic pathway for degradation (Lagace et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2007; Poirier and Mayer, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis with citation support from the literature.

claim: KPC-1 down-regulates the DMA-1 receptor through direct interaction with its extracellular domain in PVD neurons.
source: In summary, we show that KPC-1 down-regulates the DMA-1 receptor through direct interaction with its extracellular domain in PVD neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.

claim: This function of KPC-1 is necessary to allow developing dendrites to move away from the intermediate targets where the guidance cues SAX-7 and MNR-1 are highly enriched before reaching their final destinations.
source: This function is necessary to allow developing dendrites to move away from the intermediate targets where the guidance cues SAX-7 and MNR-1 are highly enriched before reaching their final destinations.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Precise regulation of receptor levels is critical for dendrite branching and patterning.
source: These results demonstrate that precise regulation of receptor levels is critical for dendrite branching and patterning.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the discussion.
